checkpoints.title: Understand Requirements
intro: Start with the central design question: **How can you combine sensors, actuators, local logic, local HMI, cloud communication, and web-based HMI into a purposeful smart system?**

blocks.title: Learning Outcomes
items: Define a real-world smart-system purpose.
Select suitable sensors and actuators.
Build a low-cost small-scale prototype.
Use local logic to make decisions from sensor evidence.
Create a local HMI for monitoring or control.
Create a web-based HMI or cloud dashboard.
Transfer data to a cloud platform or remote interface.
Explain how hardware, software, and cloud pieces interact.
Plan a project schedule and track progress.
Troubleshoot hardware, code, and interface problems systematically.
Prepare a concise proposal, demo, video, and code submission.
Use evidence to defend design decisions.
Recognize when instructor approval is required.

items.title: HMI
items.body: Local HMI required; web HMI required.

items.title: Software
items.body: LabVIEW recommended; alternatives need comparable HMI quality.

checkpoints.title: Choose Project Idea
intro: Your first submission is only one paragraph. It should name the application, the problem, at least two sensors, at least one actuator, the local HMI, and the cloud or web-based HMI.

blocks.title: One-Paragraph Template
paragraphs: Our project will design a smart `[system/application]` that solves `[real-world problem]`. It will use `[sensor 1]` and `[sensor 2]` to measure `[quantities]`, and it will control `[actuator]` to `[action]`. A local HMI will allow the user to `[monitor/control]`, while a web-based HMI will `[display/control/alert/log]` through `[cloud platform]`. The prototype will be built as a small-scale model using `[materials]`.

fields.label: Real-world problem
fields.placeholder: What problem, user, or environment is your system addressing?

fields.label: Proposed smart system
fields.placeholder: Write your one-paragraph idea draft here.

fields.label: Socratic prompts
fields.placeholder: Why is this useful? What will count as success? What could go wrong? What evidence will show it works?

items: Elevator system using limit switches and a motor.
Home security system using motion sensors.
Temperature monitoring/control system for a building.
Sun tracking system for a solar panel.
**Smart greenhouse monitor:** moisture and temperature sensors, pump or fan actuator, LabVIEW HMI, cloud dashboard. Risk: water near electronics.
**Smart package/security box:** distance and door sensors, lock or alarm actuator, web alert. Risk: mechanical reliability.
**Mini smart elevator:** limit switches, position feedback, motor actuator, HMI floor request. Risk: motor control scope.
**Smart storage monitor:** light and humidity/temperature sensing, LED/buzzer actuator, data logging. Risk: meaningful purpose.
**Solar tracker:** light sensors, servo or stepper motion, cloud status. Risk: alignment and mechanism friction.

checkpoints.title: Consult Instructor
intro: During the Nov 3 lab, the instructor spends about 5-10 minutes discussing each project idea. The idea may be accepted, modified, rejected, or replaced with a suggested direction.

items.title: Approval Check
items.body: Is the purpose clear and course-relevant?

items.title: Scope Check
items.body: Is it comparable to about three combined labs?

items.title: Risk Check
items.body: Are parts, wiring, cloud, and mechanisms realistic?

fields.label: What did the instructor approve, modify, reject, or warn about?
What must change before proposal submission?

checkpoints.title: Submit Proposal
intro: The proposal is due 09-Nov prior to lab start and should be 2-3 pages. It is the team's plan for building, testing, demonstrating, and communicating the project.

items.label: **Abstract** — Short summary of purpose and approach.
**Component list** — Sensors, actuators, Arduino, cloud, and materials.
**Electrical schematic** — Connections shown clearly; EasyEDA may be used.
**Weekly timeline** — Week-by-week hardware, software, and integration plan.

fields.label: Proposal planning prompt
fields.placeholder: What will the reader understand after two pages? What evidence will prove the design is feasible?

blocks.title: Evidence Checklist
items: System block diagram or signal path.
Electrical schematic or wiring map.
Clear sensor and actuator choices.
Local HMI and web HMI descriptions.
Cloud feature description.
Risk or troubleshooting plan.
Weekly schedule with milestones.

checkpoints.title: Build Prototype
intro: Build a low-cost, small-scale prototype. Cardboard, wood, and simple materials are acceptable when the prototype demonstrates a real smart-system purpose.

items.title: Hardware
items.body: At least two sensors and one actuator; no more than six sensors/actuators unless approved.

items.title: Purpose
items.body: The prototype should communicate a recognizable real-world application.

items.title: Instructor Role
items.body: The instructor reviews scope and monitors progress; troubleshooting remains the team's responsibility.

rangeNote.message: Missing required sensors: include at least 2 sensors.
Missing actuator: include at least 1 actuator.

checkpoints.title: Develop Local HMI
intro: A local HMI is required. LabVIEW is highly recommended, but another software environment may be accepted if the HMI quality is similar or better.

items.label: **Local HMI exists** — Students can monitor or control the system locally.
**Sufficient logic** — The program makes decisions rather than only displaying raw values.

fields.label: Local HMI controls and indicators
fields.placeholder: List the controls, indicators, modes, alarms, or settings.

checkpoints.title: Add Cloud/Web HMI
intro: The project must include a web-based HMI and a cloud feature such as data transfer, alerting, dashboard visualization, database storage, or remote control.

items.label: **Web-based HMI** — A remote dashboard or web interface is present.
**Cloud feature** — Data is transferred, logged, alerted, visualized, or used for remote control.

fields.label: Cloud and web HMI design
fields.placeholder: What variable is sent? What does the remote user see or control?

checkpoints.title: Test and Troubleshoot
intro: Attendance is required during the three project weeks. Progress is monitored and assessed, but the team is responsible for systematic troubleshooting.

blocks.title: Requirement Checker
blocks.description: This checker is a planning aid only. Instructor approval is the final decision.

blocks.title: Risk Table
rows: Too few components or weak purpose
Reconnect the build to a real use case and add meaningful sensing/actuation.
Reduce features or get instructor approval.
Build a minimal dashboard first, then improve visuals.
Test one sensor or actuator path at a time.
Prepare recorded evidence and a fallback explanation.

checkpoints.title: Prepare Demo
intro: The real-life demo happens on 24-Nov. The last hour of lab is reserved for demos only.

items.label: Software and cloud path can be explained

checkpoints.title: Record Video
intro: The video is due 24-Nov with the code submission. It should be 3-4 minutes and describe hardware, describe software, and demonstrate the main functionality.

items.body: Software: local HMI, logic, cloud, web HMI.
Summarize evidence, limitations, and final result.

blocks.title: Lab Video Submission Rubric
rows: Minimal and unclear demo of the functionalities
Most of the functionality is clearly demonstrated
Most of the hardware is clearly described
All the hardware is described and clearly explained
Most of the software is clearly described
All the software is described and clearly explained
blocks.note: The marking scheme lists Video as 2.5 marks; this rubric judges video quality and may be scaled to the official video mark.

blocks.alt: Rubric for lab video submission with criteria for demonstrating functionality, describing hardware, and describing software, scored from 0 to 3.
blocks.caption: Original rubric image from the project handout.

checkpoints.title: Submit Code and Evidence
intro: Submit the video and code by 24-Nov. Keep evidence organized so the instructor can understand what was built, how it works, and what was verified.

paragraphs: Confirm the official weighting because the handout states "Project Weight: 15 Marks" but the table totals 12.5.

fields.label: Final evidence list
fields.placeholder: List videos, code files, schematics, screenshots, measurements, and demo notes.

checkpoints.title: Reflect
intro: Use the self-assessment to see what is complete, what still needs work, and what should be confirmed with the instructor.

blocks.title: Timeline
rows: Project idea, one paragraph, due end of day.
Proposal due prior to lab start.
Execution, weekly attendance, progress monitoring, and troubleshooting.

Nearby interface such as LabVIEW front panel.
Online data transfer, storage, alerting, dashboarding, or remote control.
Design effort, integration, and functionality comparable to about three combined labs.

submissionRules: Demonstrate the working system in the lab on 24-Nov; the last hour of the lab is reserved for demos only.
Submit the 3-4 minute project video and the project code through the course LMS by 24-Nov.
Confirm the official project weighting and proposal due date in the course LMS before submitting — the dates in this workspace are planning targets.
